claim: Hard diagnostic cases are worked by generating a few hypotheses early and using them to guide data search (Elstein 1978 founding claim). It is restated, not re-measured, in later reviews; the 1978 book was not opened. Independently replicated descriptively by Barrows 1982 (37 randomly selected physicians, 62 encounters) and the McMaster group (Feightner 1977). Exact 1978 numbers still unverified.
agent_test: Compare an arm that must name 3-5 hypotheses before any data request vs a plain arm, equal tokens, on sequential-diagnosis items.
audit_note: Barrows 1982 and Feightner 1977 are the same McMaster group (Barrows, Feightner, Neufeld, Norman), Barrows also co-authored the 1978 founding work, and the Feightner 1977 abstract gives only a model, no hypothesis-generation finding, so 'independently replicated' is not supported; Barrows 1982 numbers (18+19 physicians, 62 encounters) match.

claim: Experts do not differ from novices mainly in hypothesis-testing strategy; successful and unsuccessful diagnosticians both use it, so accuracy tracks content knowledge (content specificity). Neufeld 1981 (22 students followed for years): process variables unrelated to level; only the content of hypotheses tracked level and outcome.
agent_test: Hold the scaffold fixed and vary retrieved domain knowledge; measure which contributes more to accuracy.
audit_note: Neufeld 1981 says the majority (not all) of process variables were unrelated to level; Adv Health Sci Educ 2020 defines content specificity as case-to-case performance not transferring, a related but not identical idea; Kaufman and Patel page not retrievable.

claim: Experts' edge lies in the accuracy of early hypotheses and in efficient, relevant data collection (72% of relevant findings for experts vs 45% students; 50% vs 31% of elicited findings relevant), not in asking more questions.
agent_test: Score hypothesis quality and relevant-finding share per question in agent transcripts, not question count.

claim: Number of early hypotheses rose with training in one small McGill study (1.5, 3, 3.4, resident 5), which cuts against the review claim that experts generate no more hypotheses.
agent_test: Count early candidates in strong vs weak model runs; check if candidate count predicts accuracy.

claim: In a small think-aloud study (Arocha and Patel 1991; 4 participants per group plus one resident, figures not independently checked) cues were mostly used as confirming (71% to 92%) and all second-year students kept their initial hypothesis despite contradictory data; for LLMs, authors report qualitatively that an off-the-shelf o3 baseline seemed to anchor on first impressions (Nori 2025), and a multi-agent GPT-4 setup raised top-diagnosis accuracy from 0/80 to 71.3% on 16 bias-driven misdiagnosis cases (Ke 2024), but plain-model anchoring was not measured.
agent_test: Insert a contradicting finding mid-case; measure revision rate with and without a mandatory disconfirm step.
audit_note: Arocha and Patel page could not be opened (blocked); the LLM part rests on one qualitative remark that o3 'seemed to anchor' (Nori) and Ke's 0/80 initial accuracy on case reports selected for bias-driven misdiagnosis, neither of which measures anchoring in plain LLMs.
claim_before_audit: Students mostly confirm their first hypothesis (71% to 92% of cues used as confirming); all second-year students kept the initial hypothesis despite contradictory data. Plain LLMs show the same anchoring.

claim: An orchestrator with explicit hypothesis tracking and a challenger role raised accuracy of a strong LLM (o3 78.6% to 81.9%; budgeted 79.9% at about 70% lower cost than bare o3) and generalised across 6 model families (about +11 points average). Roles were not ablated. Gap search: the paper has no role ablation (variants differ in budget, ensembling and question-only modes; single vs batched both 83.9%); no third-party ablation found.
agent_test: Ablate roles one at a time at matched cost on sequential-diagnosis cases.

claim: Prompting a model to use differential-diagnosis style reasoning does not reliably beat plain chain of thought: GPT-4 +2.2 points (p=0.24); GPT-3.5 -8 points (p<0.001). a25, b05 and c08 are one study.
agent_test: Replicate on a current model family with identical token budgets.

claim: Telling clinicians to slow down and reflect does not raise accuracy (44.5% speed vs 45.0% reflect, residents); self-directed second looks revise only 8% of diagnoses for +0.02 of 2 points.
agent_test: Compare a generic reconsider prompt to a no-op second pass at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Structured checklists or forced analysis of the initial impression help, including experts (nephrologists 31.1% to 65.6%; checklists corrected 0.29 vs 0.03 errors per ECG), but designs lack a no-intervention control. Bass 2013 reopened (abstract): N=15, no no-priming control, p=0.07 beside an OR whose CI excludes 1.
agent_test: Run a structured re-check vs unstructured re-check vs none, at equal tokens, on ambiguous cases.

claim: Pure hypothetico-deductive reasoning had lower odds of success than pattern recognition or scheme-inductive reasoning in think-aloud studies, but strategy was coded after the fact and may follow case ease.
agent_test: Give the agent a fast path for easy items and a full loop for hard items; compare to always-loop at equal tokens.

claim: In the LDTL preprint (Llama-3-8B, MIMIC-CDM), a random test-selection planner scored 84.8% (85.4 +- 1.3 over 5 seeds), above the prompted ReAct agent (74.9) and the trained hypothesis-driven LA-CDM (81.3) as reported by the LA-CDM authors; only LDTL's learned planner (93.4) beat random clearly. This random-planner comparison comes from one preprint and was not independently replicated.
agent_test: Always include a random-test baseline when evaluating a hypothesis-driven test selector.
audit_note: All numbers match, but the random-planner score (84.8; 85.4 +- 1.3 over 5 seeds) appears only in the LDTL preprint, whose LA-CDM and ReAct numbers are copied from the LA-CDM paper, so this is a single-source cross-paper comparison, not independent confirmation; Hager does not test a random planner.
claim_before_audit: Hypothesis-driven LLM diagnosis is not clearly better than random test choice on MIMIC-CDM: random planner 84.8 vs prompted ReAct 74.9 vs hypothesis-driven LA-CDM 81.3; only a learned planner reached 93.4.

claim: Choosing tests by expected uncertainty reduction (simulated results, Bayesian design) beat LLM-chosen tests; an external guideline planner fixed open models that could not run their own questioning.
agent_test: Replace the agent's test pick with an explicit expected-information-gain step at equal call count.

claim: LLMs asked to ask follow-up questions get worse unless they can abstain: -11.3% vs asking none; abstention with rationale and self-consistency +22.3% over the interactive baseline.
agent_test: Test an abstain-or-ask gate with calibrated confidence vs always ask.
audit_note: The 11.3% drop is a relative drop versus the non-interactive Initial setting (not versus no information), and 22.3% is relative to the basic interactive setup; only MediQ directly supports the abstention claim, Hager is context.

claim: Hypothesis-test loops fail in LLMs in recurring ways: tests not tied to stated hypotheses, erratic belief updates, lost state; divergent belief updates after tests fell from 15.2% to 4.6% after trajectory-consistency training.
agent_test: Log hypothesis-to-test links in agent traces and count unlinked tests; add a link-check guard.

claim: An LLM alone lists the right diagnosis in its top 10 more often than unassisted clinicians (59.1% vs 33.6%) and helps clinicians' lists (51.7% vs 36.1%), but giving physicians a chatbot did not raise case-level reasoning scores (76% vs 74%, CI -4 to 8) while the LLM alone scored 16 points higher.
agent_test: Measure top-k recall of the candidate list separately from final accuracy.

claim: Cognitive-bias prompts degrade LLM medical accuracy (GPT-4 up to -14 points on false consensus; larger average drops for weaker models); reasoning variants are not reliably robust, though debiasing instructions and few-shot examples cut biased answers.
agent_test: Run a bias-injection set (anchor, confirmation) with and without guard text at equal tokens, using unpublished prompts.

claim: Instructions to generate many or few hypotheses, early or late, had no effect on outcome (N=30 students, Sprafka 1973); only a secondhand search-snippet summary was seen. Gap search: MSU repository blocked the primary text; still secondhand.
agent_test: Vary the number of hypotheses requested (1, 3, 6) at equal tokens.

claim: Early hypotheses are often accurate; the split between high- and low-knowledge physicians is in evaluation: high-knowledge physicians generated accurate hypotheses early and spent the rest confirming or discarding alternatives.
agent_test: Spend the token budget on discriminating tests rather than on more candidates; compare allocations.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In the human literature, forward reasoning (data to hypothesis) went with higher accuracy, while backward (hypothesis to data) reasoning was tied to working-memory load and failure.
agent_test: Compare forward vs backward prompts at equal tokens.

claim: Hypothetico-deductive structure plus knowledge both matter for LLMs: removing the knowledge graph cost 25.5 points (69.8 to 44.3) and random instead of information-gain question choice cost 38.7 points on MedKGI (Qwen3-8B); ClinicalAgents shows memory and hypothesis-backtracking each add about 2.4-4.4 points on GPT-5.2 (average 0.452 to 0.511 combined). No study crosses scaffold on/off with knowledge on/off in one design.
agent_test: 2x2: scaffold on/off x retrieved disease knowledge on/off at equal tokens.

claim: Accuracy as a function of number of candidate hypotheses peaks near 5 in one LLM pipeline (MedKGI, Qwen3-8B) and falls with more; no frontier-model or human replication (Sprafka 1973 primary text not reachable).
agent_test: Request 1, 3, 5, 8 hypotheses at equal tokens on a held-out sequential set.

claim: No ablation isolates any MAI-DxO role; the only ablation in the paper is single vs batched questioning (both 83.9%). Which role carries the gain is unknown.
agent_test: Drop one role at a time at matched cost.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs commit prematurely when information is insufficient: about 70% false action when the right option is removed (55-82% by model on MedQA), 81% premature closure on underspecified low-risk cases vs 19% on urgent ones, and a safety prompt lowers false action to about 48%, not to zero (Handler et al. 2026). In VivaBench multi-turn exams, approximate (lenient) top-1 accuracy of about 0.90-0.94 with full information falls to 0.65-0.75 after data gathering across six models, and exact top-1 for the best model falls from 69% to 35%.
agent_test: Abstain-or-ask gate calibrated on case difficulty; measure false-action rate.
audit_note: The 0.93 to 0.65-0.75 figures are correct but are VivaBench's approximate (lenient) top-1 accuracy from appendix Table 8 (six models, full information 0.90-0.94, final 0.65-0.75); the main-text exact top-1 for the best model is 35% final vs 69% full information, a larger relative fall, and the metric is not labelled in the claim. Premature-closure numbers match.
claim_before_audit: LLMs commit prematurely when information is insufficient and are poor at detecting it: about 70% false action when the right option is removed (55-82% by model), 81% premature closure on underspecified low-risk cases vs 19% on urgent ones; a safety prompt lowers it to about 48%, not to zero. In multi-turn exams, accuracy given full information (about 0.93) falls to 0.65-0.75 after data gathering.

claim: A bias-correcting multi-agent debate rescued 71.3% of top diagnoses (57/80) from a wrong initial answer, but cases were selected for being initially wrong and no equal-token control exists, so the effect of an explicit disconfirmation step is untested.
agent_test: Disconfirmation step on/off at equal tokens on unpublished bias cases.
